title: v1/chat: stabilize streaming handshake; enforce stop-token precedence and introduce role-alias mapping
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Customers integrating via the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface have seen two classes of issues in production: 1) transient stream disconnects during tool/function call handoffs (client resumes see inconsistent framing), and 2) ambiguity in how stop tokens are applied when stop arrays are provided alongside role-level stop hints or tool-generated token sequences. This PR unifies several compatibility behaviors to reduce surprise for downstream clients and to harden streaming handshakes during function/tool call routing. Motivation: Provide predictable, backward-compatible semantics for v1 chat parity while reducing the failure surface during streaming toolcalls. Goals: (a) stabilize the streaming handshake so that tool/function call initiation and the subsequent resumption of the assistant stream never produce overlapping or dropped deltas, (b) define and implement a deterministic stop-token precedence order (explicit request param > tool-produced stop sequence > role-level hints), (c) add an opt-in role_alias mapping so customers sending alternative role names (e.g., "assistant_bot", "system_agent") map to canonical OpenAI roles for compatibility, and (d) wrap logprobs and structured scores in a deterministic envelope that matches OpenAI parity expectations when streaming deltas are emitted. Changes: - runtime/stream: implement a two-phase handshake for toolcall handoff with explicit ACK/FIN markers and idempotent resume tokens so retries do not duplicate tokens - api/openai_compat: introduce a stop precedence resolver that accepts stop arrays and role/tool hints and returns the canonical stop set applied to generation - api/openai_compat: add role_alias config parsing and mapping; default mappings included and overridable via server config - models/compat: attach a small envelope to streaming delta messages: choices[].delta.{content,role,tool_call,logprobs} to avoid ambiguous flattened fields - sdk/python: update OpenAI-compat adapter to accept role_alias and expose resolved_stop in response metadata - tests: new integration tests exercising stream resume, stop precedence and role aliasing Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is backward-compatible; the stop precedence policy is additive and only changes behavior when multiple stop sources are present (rare). Role-alias mapping is opt-in per-tenant via configuration flag; we set sane defaults for common aliases. The streaming handshake change is released behind a runtime feature-flag; feature is enabled for canary tenants and then rolled out to all after 72h of telemetry. Checklist: [x] unit tests for precedence resolver [x] integration test for stream resume [x] SDK adapter updates [x] e2e smoke in Canary [x] docs note in openai/v1_chat.md Testing: CI includes unit and integration runs. Canary telemetry evaluated for token duplication and error rates for 72h. Observability: added new metrics stream.handshake_retries, stream.duplicate_delta_count, compat.role_alias_mappings_applied Related: ENG-1542 (stream stability), ENG-1588 (openai compat stop semantics), SUP-4321 customer report Refs: docs/openai/v1_chat.md, runtime/stream/README.md

release_notes:
- Stabilize streaming handshake for tool/function handoffs to prevent duplicated or dropped deltas.
- Define stop-token precedence (explicit param > tool sequences > role hints) to remove ambiguity in mixed stop sources.
- Add role_alias mapping to improve compatibility with non-canonical role names from third-party clients.
- Emit structured logprobs in choices[].delta.logprobs during streaming to match OpenAI parity formats.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'enable_chatv1_stream_handshake_v2'; enable in Canary first. Monitor metrics: stream.handshake_retries, stream.duplicate_delta_count. Rollback: disable feature flag and invalidate resume tokens by bumping resume-token-salt. Estimated rollout impact: low, opt-in role alias mapping disabled by default for enterprise tenants.
risk_assessment: Medium: changes affect runtime message framing and stop semantics. Mitigations include feature flag, canary rollout, and conservative default stop precedence. Extensive unit/integration tests added.
testing_summary: Local unit tests: 98/98 passing. Integration test suite: 24 new tests added; CI run after fixes: all green. Canary telemetry evaluated for 72h before full rollout. Manual smoke tested with python sdk adapter examples.
